sanskrit: ṛ̱tur jani̍trī̱ tasyā̍ a̱pas pari̍ ma̱kṣū jā̱ta āvi̍śa̱d yāsu̱ vardha̍te | tad ā̍ha̱nā a̍bhavat pi̱pyuṣī̱ payo̱ 'ṁśoḥ pī̱yūṣa̍m pratha̱maṁ tad u̱kthya̍m ||
english: She who is the birth-season, his mother — around her waters he was swiftly born, in whom he grows. That which became swollen, brimming with milk: the first-pressed nectar of the soma-stalk — that is praiseworthy.

sanskrit: sa̱dhrīm ā ya̍nti̱ pari̱ bibhra̍tī̱ḥ payo̍ vi̱śvapsnyā̍ya̱ pra bha̍ranta̱ bhoja̍nam | sa̱mā̱no adhvā̍ pra̱vatā̍m anu̱ṣyade̱ yas tākṛ̍ṇoḥ pratha̱maṁ sāsy u̱kthya̍ḥ ||
english: Together they come, bearing milk in abundance, bearing nourishment for universal enjoyment. One road runs downward along the slopes — he who first made these things, thou art praiseworthy.

sanskrit: anv eko̍ vadati̱ yad dadā̍ti̱ tad rū̱pā mi̱nan tada̍pā̱ eka̍ īyate | viśvā̱ eka̍sya vi̱nuda̍s titikṣate̱ yas tākṛ̍ṇoḥ pratha̱maṁ sāsy u̱kthya̍ḥ ||
english: The one speaks after, whatever he gives; the other, fashioning forms, moves by means of water. All things endure the impulse of the one — he who first made these things, thou art praiseworthy.

sanskrit: pra̱jābhya̍ḥ pu̱ṣṭiṁ vi̱bhaja̍nta āsate ra̱yim i̍va pṛ̱ṣṭham pra̱bhava̍ntam āya̱te | asi̍nva̱n daṁṣṭrai̍ḥ pi̱tur a̍tti̱ bhoja̍na̱ṁ yas tākṛ̍ṇoḥ pratha̱maṁ sāsy u̱kthya̍ḥ ||
english: They sit distributing nourishment to creatures, like wealth upon the back of one who waxes great as he comes. With unsatiated fangs he eats the father's food — he who first made these things, thou art praiseworthy.

sanskrit: adhā̍kṛṇoḥ pṛthi̱vīṁ sa̱ṁdṛśe̍ di̱ve yo dhau̍tī̱nām a̍hiha̱nn āri̍ṇak pa̱thaḥ | taṁ tvā̱ stome̍bhir u̱dabhi̱r na vā̱jina̍ṁ de̱vaṁ de̱vā a̍jana̱n sāsy u̱kthya̍ḥ ||
english: Then thou madest the earth to be seen by heaven — thou who, slaying the serpent of the torrents, didst open the paths. The gods begat thee, like a mighty steed, to be hymned with praises and with waters — thou art praiseworthy.

sanskrit: yo bhoja̍naṁ ca̱ daya̍se ca̱ vardha̍nam ā̱rdrād ā śuṣka̱m madhu̍mad du̱dohi̍tha | sa śe̍va̱dhiṁ ni da̍dhiṣe vi̱vasva̍ti̱ viśva̱syaika̍ īśiṣe̱ sāsy u̱kthya̍ḥ ||
english: Thou who dispensest nourishment and growth, who hast milked out honey-sweetness from the moist and dry alike — thou layest up treasure in the realm of the sun; thou alone art lord of all — thou art praiseworthy.

sanskrit: yaḥ pu̱ṣpiṇī̍ś ca pra̱sva̍ś ca̱ dharma̱ṇādhi̱ dāne̱ vy a1̱̍vanī̱r adhā̍rayaḥ | yaś cāsa̍mā̱ aja̍no di̱dyuto̍ di̱va u̱rur ū̱rvām̐ a̱bhita̱ḥ sāsy u̱kthya̍ḥ ||
english: Thou who, by ordinance, didst hold up the blossoming and the fertile streams at their bestowing, who didst create unequal beings blazing from heaven, the wide wide-spreading on every side — thou art praiseworthy.

sanskrit: yo nā̍rma̱raṁ sa̱hava̍su̱ṁ niha̍ntave pṛ̱kṣāya̍ ca dā̱save̍śāya̱ cāva̍haḥ | ū̱rjaya̍ntyā̱ apa̍riviṣṭam ā̱sya̍m u̱taivādya pu̍rukṛ̱t sāsy u̱kthya̍ḥ ||
english: Thou who didst bring down Nārmarī together with his wealth, for the slaying and for the gift of Dāsaveśa — the mouth encompassed by the strength-bestowing one, and even today, O much-doer, thou art praiseworthy.

sanskrit: śa̱taṁ vā̱ yasya̱ daśa̍ sā̱kam ādya̱ eka̍sya śru̱ṣṭau yad dha̍ co̱dam āvi̍tha | a̱ra̱jjau dasyū̱n sam u̍nab da̱bhīta̍ye suprā̱vyo̍ abhava̱ḥ sāsy u̱kthya̍ḥ ||
english: Whose hundred, even ten, eating together at once — at the summons of one alone didst thou indeed spur them forth. Thou didst bind the Dasyus without a rope for Dabhīti's sake; thou becamest most helpful — thou art praiseworthy.

sanskrit: viśved anu̍ rodha̱nā a̍sya̱ pauṁsya̍ṁ da̱dur a̍smai dadhi̱re kṛ̱tnave̱ dhana̍m | ṣaḻ a̍stabhnā vi̱ṣṭira̱ḥ pañca̍ sa̱ṁdṛśa̱ḥ pari̍ pa̱ro a̍bhava̱ḥ sāsy u̱kthya̍ḥ ||
english: All things followed the blockings of his manly power; they gave him treasure, they assigned wealth to the effective one. Thou didst prop up six expanses, five visible ones; thou becamest the encompassing beyond — thou art praiseworthy.

sanskrit: su̱pra̱vā̱ca̱naṁ tava̍ vīra vī̱rya1̱̍ṁ yad eke̍na̱ kratu̍nā vi̱ndase̱ vasu̍ | jā̱tūṣṭhi̍rasya̱ pra vaya̱ḥ saha̍svato̱ yā ca̱kartha̱ sendra̱ viśvā̍sy u̱kthya̍ḥ ||
english: Well worth proclaiming is thy heroic valour, O hero, whereby with a single will thou findest goods. The might of Jātuṣṭhira the powerful dost thou increase — all that thou hast done, together with Indra, is praiseworthy.

sanskrit: ara̍maya̱ḥ sara̍pasa̱s tarā̍ya̱ kaṁ tu̱rvīta̍ye ca va̱yyā̍ya ca sru̱tim | nī̱cā santa̱m ud a̍nayaḥ parā̱vṛja̱m prāndhaṁ śro̱ṇaṁ śra̍vayan sa̱sy u̱kthya̍ḥ ||
english: Thou didst clear the road of those without horses and without provisions for Turvīta and for Vayya to cross. One cast down low, a cripple, thou didst raise him up; making the blind and the lame to hear — thou art praiseworthy.

sanskrit: a̱smabhya̱ṁ tad va̍so dā̱nāya̱ rādha̍ḥ sam a̍rthayasva ba̱hu te̍ vasa̱vya̍m | indra̱ yac ci̱traṁ śra̍va̱syā anu̱ dyūn bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: Concentrate for us that wealth for giving, O Lord of wealth; great is thy richness. Indra, with the glittering renown through the days — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.

sanskrit: adhva̍ryavo̱ bhara̱tendrā̍ya̱ soma̱m āma̍trebhiḥ siñcatā̱ madya̱m andha̍ḥ | kā̱mī hi vī̱raḥ sada̍m asya pī̱tiṁ ju̱hota̱ vṛṣṇe̱ tad id e̱ṣa va̍ṣṭi ||
english: O Adhvaryus, bring soma for Indra; pour the intoxicating draught into the vessels. The hero ever desires his drink — offer it to the bull; this very thing he craves.

sanskrit: adhva̍ryavo̱ yo a̱po va̍vri̱vāṁsa̍ṁ vṛ̱traṁ ja̱ghānā̱śanye̍va vṛ̱kṣam | tasmā̍ e̱tam bha̍rata tadva̱śāya̍m̐ e̱ṣa indro̍ arhati pī̱tim a̍sya ||
english: O Adhvaryus, he who smote Vṛtra that had wrapped the waters round, as lightning strikes a tree — bring this soma to him who wills it so; Indra is worthy of drinking this.

sanskrit: adhva̍ryavo̱ yo dṛbhī̍kaṁ ja̱ghāna̱ yo gā u̱dāja̱d apa̱ hi va̱laṁ vaḥ | tasmā̍ e̱tam a̱ntari̍kṣe̱ na vāta̱m indra̱ṁ somai̱r orṇu̍ta̱ jūr na vastrai̍ḥ ||
english: O Adhvaryus, he who slew Dṛbhīka, who drove out the cows, who cleft Vala for you — him, Indra, wrap in somas as the midair wraps the wind, as a woman wraps in garments.

sanskrit: adhva̍ryavo̱ ya ura̍ṇaṁ ja̱ghāna̱ nava̍ ca̱khvāṁsa̍ṁ nava̱tiṁ ca̍ bā̱hūn | yo arbu̍da̱m ava̍ nī̱cā ba̍bā̱dhe tam indra̱ṁ soma̍sya bhṛ̱the hi̍nota ||
english: O Adhvaryus, he who slew Uraṇa gnawing with ninety and nine arms, who drove Arbuda downward low — urge that Indra on at the pressing of the soma.

sanskrit: adhva̍ryavo̱ yaḥ sv aśna̍ṁ ja̱ghāna̱ yaḥ śuṣṇa̍m a̱śuṣa̱ṁ yo vya̍ṁsam | yaḥ pipru̱ṁ namu̍ci̱ṁ yo ru̍dhi̱krāṁ tasmā̱ indrā̱yāndha̍so juhota ||
english: O Adhvaryus, he who slew Svaśna, who slew Śuṣṇa the shriveller and Vyaṁsa, who slew Pipru, Namuci, and Rudhikrā — pour the soma for that Indra.

sanskrit: adhva̍ryavo̱ yaḥ śa̱taṁ śamba̍rasya̱ puro̍ bi̱bhedāśma̍neva pū̱rvīḥ | yo va̱rcina̍ḥ śa̱tam indra̍ḥ sa̱hasra̍m a̱pāva̍pa̱d bhara̍tā̱ soma̍m asmai ||
english: O Adhvaryus, he who pierced the hundred strongholds of Śambara as if they were ancient stones, who felled a hundred, a thousand of the Varcinas — O Bharatas, offer soma to him.

sanskrit: adhva̍ryavo̱ yaḥ śa̱tam ā sa̱hasra̱m bhūmyā̍ u̱pasthe 'va̍paj jagha̱nvān | kutsa̍syā̱yor a̍tithi̱gvasya̍ vī̱rān ny āvṛ̍ṇa̱g bhara̍tā̱ soma̍m asmai ||
english: O Adhvaryus, he who, having slain, felled a hundred, a thousand in the lap of earth — who turned back the heroes of Kutsa, Āyu, and Atithigva — O Bharatas, offer soma to him.

sanskrit: adhva̍ryavo̱ yan na̍raḥ kā̱mayā̍dhve śru̱ṣṭī vaha̍nto naśathā̱ tad indre̍ | gabha̍stipūtam bharata śru̱tāyendrā̍ya̱ soma̍ṁ yajyavo juhota ||
english: O Adhvaryus, whatever ye men desire, bringing obedience, ye shall attain that in Indra. Bring the soma purified in the palms, O worshippers; pour it for Indra who is famed.

sanskrit: adhva̍ryava̱ḥ karta̍nā śru̱ṣṭim a̍smai̱ vane̱ nipū̍ta̱ṁ vana̱ un na̍yadhvam | ju̱ṣā̱ṇo hastya̍m a̱bhi vā̍vaśe va̱ indrā̍ya̱ soma̍m madi̱raṁ ju̍hota ||
english: O Adhvaryus, bestow obedience upon him; from the wood bring up what has been purified in the wood. Delighting in what is offered by hand, he calls to you — pour the exhilarating soma for Indra.

sanskrit: adhva̍ryava̱ḥ paya̱sodha̱r yathā̱ goḥ some̍bhir īm pṛṇatā bho̱jam indra̍m | vedā̱ham a̍sya̱ nibhṛ̍tam ma e̱tad ditsa̍nta̱m bhūyo̍ yaja̱taś ci̍keta ||
english: O Adhvaryus, as the udder of a cow with milk, fill Indra the enjoyer with somas. I know his secret — this very one wishes to give more; may the adorable one take note of it.

sanskrit: adhva̍ryavo̱ yo di̱vyasya̱ vasvo̱ yaḥ pārthi̍vasya̱ kṣamya̍sya̱ rājā̍ | tam ūrda̍ra̱ṁ na pṛ̍ṇatā̱ yave̱nendra̱ṁ some̍bhi̱s tad apo̍ vo astu ||
english: O Adhvaryus, he who is king of heavenly wealth, of earthly wealth, of terrestrial wealth — fill him, Indra, like a belly with barley-somas; so let it be of benefit to you.

sanskrit: a̱smabhya̱ṁ tad va̍so dā̱nāya̱ rādha̍ḥ sam a̍rthayasva ba̱hu te̍ vasa̱vya̍m | indra̱ yac ci̱traṁ śra̍va̱syā anu̱ dyūn bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: Concentrate for us that wealth for giving, O Lord of wealth; great is thy richness. Indra, with the glittering renown through the days — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.

sanskrit: pra ghā̱ nv a̍sya maha̱to ma̱hāni̍ sa̱tyā sa̱tyasya̱ kara̍ṇāni vocam | trika̍drukeṣv apibat su̱tasyā̱sya made̱ ahi̱m indro̍ jaghāna ||
english: Now indeed let me proclaim the great and true deeds of this great one, the acts of accomplishment of the truthful one. At the three Trikadrukas he drank of the pressed soma — in the rapture of this, Indra slew the serpent.

sanskrit: a̱va̱ṁśe dyām a̍stabhāyad bṛ̱hanta̱m ā roda̍sī apṛṇad a̱ntari̍kṣam | sa dhā̍rayat pṛthi̱vīm pa̱pratha̍c ca̱ soma̍sya̱ tā mada̱ indra̍ś cakāra ||
english: He propped up the vast sky without a prop; he filled the two world-halves and the atmosphere. He held up the earth and spread it wide — these things Indra did in the rapture of soma.

sanskrit: sadme̍va̱ prāco̱ vi mi̍māya̱ mānai̱r vajre̍ṇa̱ khāny a̍tṛṇan na̱dīnā̍m | vṛthā̍sṛjat pa̱thibhi̍r dīrghayā̱thaiḥ soma̍sya̱ tā mada̱ indra̍ś cakāra ||
english: He measured out the eastern regions as if they were a dwelling, with his bolt he pierced the channels of the rivers. He set them free along paths running far — these things Indra did in the rapture of soma.

sanskrit: sa pra̍vo̱ḻhṝn pa̍ri̱gatyā̍ da̱bhīte̱r viśva̍m adhā̱g āyu̍dham i̱ddhe a̱gnau | saṁ gobhi̱r aśvai̍r asṛja̱d rathe̍bhi̱ḥ soma̍sya̱ tā mada̱ indra̍ś cakāra ||
english: He brought to naught those who had carried off Dabhīti's possessions; he placed all weapons into the blazing fire. He released cattle, horses, and chariots — these things Indra did in the rapture of soma.

sanskrit: sa ī̍m ma̱hīṁ dhuni̱m eto̍r aramṇā̱t so a̍snā̱tṝn a̍pārayat sva̱sti | ta u̱tsnāya̍ ra̱yim a̱bhi pra ta̍sthu̱ḥ soma̍sya̱ tā mada̱ indra̍ś cakāra ||
english: He stilled the great roaring flood of Ita; he brought those who could not swim safely across. They went forward to him who had bathed in wealth — these things Indra did in the rapture of soma.

sanskrit: soda̍ñca̱ṁ sindhu̍m ariṇān mahi̱tvā vajre̱ṇāna̍ u̱ṣasa̱ḥ sam pi̍peṣa | a̱ja̱vaso̍ ja̱vinī̍bhir vivṛ̱ścan soma̍sya̱ tā mada̱ indra̍ś cakāra ||
english: He let the Sindhu flow northward by his greatness; with his bolt he crushed together the cloud before the dawn. He hewed asunder the swift ones with his swift steeds — these things Indra did in the rapture of soma.

sanskrit: sa vi̱dvām̐ a̍pago̱haṁ ka̱nīnā̍m ā̱vir bhava̱nn ud a̍tiṣṭhat parā̱vṛk | prati̍ śro̱ṇaḥ sthā̱d vy a1̱̍nag a̍caṣṭa̱ soma̍sya̱ tā mada̱ indra̍ś cakāra ||
english: Knowing the concealed retreat of the maidens, he rose up manifest, having turned back. The lame stood upright, the blind looked with open eyes — these things Indra did in the rapture of soma.

sanskrit: bhi̱nad va̱lam aṅgi̍robhir gṛṇā̱no vi parva̍tasya dṛṁhi̱tāny ai̍rat | ri̱ṇag rodhā̍ṁsi kṛ̱trimā̍ṇy eṣā̱ṁ soma̍sya̱ tā mada̱ indra̍ś cakāra ||
english: Praised by the Aṅgirases, he clove Vala; he shattered the firm fortifications of the mountain. He loosed the artificial barriers of those waters — these things Indra did in the rapture of soma.

sanskrit: svapne̍nā̱bhyupyā̱ cumu̍ri̱ṁ dhuni̍ṁ ca ja̱ghantha̱ dasyu̱m pra da̱bhīti̍m āvaḥ | ra̱mbhī ci̱d atra̍ vivide̱ hira̍ṇya̱ṁ soma̍sya̱ tā mada̱ indra̍ś cakāra ||
english: Lulling Cumuri and Dhuni to sleep thou didst smite them, the Dasyus; thou didst protect Dabhīti. Even the lame one found gold here — these things Indra did in the rapture of soma.

sanskrit: nū̱naṁ sā te̱ prati̱ vara̍ṁ jari̱tre du̍hī̱yad i̍ndra̱ dakṣi̍ṇā ma̱ghonī̍ | śikṣā̍ sto̱tṛbhyo̱ māti̍ dha̱g bhago̍ no bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: Now may that generous dakshinā of thine, O Indra, yield to the singer in return for his choice. Be bountiful to the praisers; let not our fortune be consumed — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.

sanskrit: pra va̍ḥ sa̱tāṁ jyeṣṭha̍tamāya suṣṭu̱tim a̱gnāv i̍va samidhā̱ne ha̱vir bha̍re | indra̍m aju̱ryaṁ ja̱raya̍ntam ukṣi̱taṁ sa̱nād yuvā̍na̱m ava̍se havāmahe ||
english: For you the best among the true, I bring praise as an oblation on a kindled fire. We invoke Indra, unaging, yet making others age, well-nourished, forever young, for our help.

sanskrit: yasmā̱d indrā̍d bṛha̱taḥ kiṁ ca̱nem ṛ̱te viśvā̍ny asmi̱n sambhṛ̱tādhi̍ vī̱ryā̍ | ja̱ṭhare̱ soma̍ṁ ta̱nvī̱3̱̍ saho̱ maho̱ haste̱ vajra̱m bhara̍ti śī̱rṣaṇi̱ kratu̍m ||
english: From great Indra, what is there apart? All heroic powers are gathered in him. In his belly he carries soma, in his body great strength, in his hand the thunderbolt, on his head wisdom.

sanskrit: na kṣo̱ṇībhyā̍m pari̱bhve̍ ta indri̱yaṁ na sa̍mu̱draiḥ parva̍tair indra te̱ ratha̍ḥ | na te̱ vajra̱m anv a̍śnoti̱ kaś ca̱na yad ā̱śubhi̱ḥ pata̍si̱ yoja̍nā pu̱ru ||
english: By the two world-halves thy might is not encompassed, nor by the seas, nor by the mountains thy chariot, O Indra. No one overtakes thy thunderbolt when thou fliest with thy swift horses across many leagues.

sanskrit: viśve̱ hy a̍smai yaja̱tāya̍ dhṛ̱ṣṇave̱ kratu̱m bhara̍nti vṛṣa̱bhāya̱ saśca̍te | vṛṣā̍ yajasva ha̱viṣā̍ vi̱duṣṭa̍ra̱ḥ pibe̍ndra̱ soma̍ṁ vṛṣa̱bheṇa̍ bhā̱nunā̍ ||
english: All beings bring will-power to this bold and adorable one, the bull who is incessant. Worship, O bull, with oblation — thou who art wiser; drink, Indra, the soma with bull-like brilliance.

sanskrit: vṛṣṇa̱ḥ kośa̍ḥ pavate̱ madhva̍ ū̱rmir vṛ̍ṣa̱bhānnā̍ya vṛṣa̱bhāya̱ pāta̍ve | vṛṣa̍ṇādhva̱ryū vṛ̍ṣa̱bhāso̱ adra̍yo̱ vṛṣa̍ṇa̱ṁ soma̍ṁ vṛṣa̱bhāya̍ suṣvati ||
english: The sack of the bull flows, a wave of honey, for the bull to eat and for the bull to drink. The two bull-like Adhvaryus, the bull-like stones press out the bull-like soma for the bull.

sanskrit: vṛṣā̍ te̱ vajra̍ u̱ta te̱ vṛṣā̱ ratho̱ vṛṣa̍ṇā̱ harī̍ vṛṣa̱bhāṇy āyu̍dhā | vṛṣṇo̱ mada̍sya vṛṣabha̱ tvam ī̍śiṣa̱ indra̱ soma̍sya vṛṣa̱bhasya̍ tṛpṇuhi ||
english: Bull-like is thy thunderbolt and bull-like thy chariot, thy two bay horses are bulls, bull-like are thy weapons. Of the bull-like rapture, O bull, thou art lord — satiate thyself, Indra, with the bull-like soma.

sanskrit: pra te̱ nāva̱ṁ na sama̍ne vaca̱syuva̱m brahma̍ṇā yāmi̱ sava̍neṣu̱ dādhṛ̍ṣiḥ | ku̱vin no̍ a̱sya vaca̍so ni̱bodhi̍ṣa̱d indra̱m utsa̱ṁ na vasu̍naḥ sicāmahe ||
english: I advance toward thee with a prayer, like a boat on a field of battle, bold at the pressings. May he hearken to this our word — may we pour out Indra like a spring of wealth.

sanskrit: pu̱rā sa̍mbā̱dhād a̱bhy ā va̍vṛtsva no dhe̱nur na va̱tsaṁ yava̍sasya pi̱pyuṣī̍ | sa̱kṛt su te̍ suma̱tibhi̍ḥ śatakrato̱ sam patnī̍bhi̱r na vṛṣa̍ṇo nasīmahi ||
english: Turn back to us before the press of need, as a cow full of milk turns to her calf in the pasture. O thou of a hundred plans, even once with thy graces may we meet, as with consorts the bull-like one.

sanskrit: nū̱naṁ sā te̱ prati̱ vara̍ṁ jari̱tre du̍hī̱yad i̍ndra̱ dakṣi̍ṇā ma̱ghonī̍ | śikṣā̍ sto̱tṛbhyo̱ māti̍ dha̱g bhago̍ no bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: Now may that generous dakshinā of thine, O Indra, yield to the singer in return for his choice. Be bountiful to the praisers; let not our fortune be consumed — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.

sanskrit: tad a̍smai̱ navya̍m aṅgira̱svad a̍rcata̱ śuṣmā̱ yad a̍sya pra̱tnatho̱dīra̍te | viśvā̱ yad go̱trā saha̍sā̱ parī̍vṛtā̱ made̱ soma̍sya dṛṁhi̱tāny aira̍yat ||
english: Sing to him this fresh hymn as the Aṅgirases did, as his ancient strength is stirred. When in the rapture of soma he shook loose all the fortifications of the cattle-pen surrounded by force on all sides.

sanskrit: sa bhū̍tu̱ yo ha̍ pratha̱māya̱ dhāya̍sa̱ ojo̱ mimā̍no mahi̱māna̱m āti̍rat | śūro̱ yo yu̱tsu ta̱nva̍m pari̱vyata̍ śī̱rṣaṇi̱ dyām ma̍hi̱nā praty a̍muñcata ||
english: Let him be praised who, for the first nutriment, measuring out his might, surpassed greatness — the hero who in battle wrapt his body around, and by his greatness adorned the sky upon his head.

sanskrit: adhā̍kṛṇoḥ pratha̱maṁ vī̱rya̍m ma̱had yad a̱syāgre̱ brahma̍ṇā̱ śuṣma̱m aira̍yaḥ | ra̱the̱ṣṭhena̱ harya̍śvena̱ vicyu̍tā̱ḥ pra jī̱raya̍ḥ sisrate sa̱dhrya1̱̍k pṛtha̍k ||
english: Then thou didst perform the first great heroic deed, when thou didst rouse the mighty impulse before this with thy prayer. Shaken loose by him standing in the chariot with his bay horses, the swift ones rush forward together and apart.

sanskrit: adhā̱ yo viśvā̱ bhuva̍nā̱bhi ma̱jmane̍śāna̱kṛt prava̍yā a̱bhy ava̍rdhata | ād roda̍sī̱ jyoti̍ṣā̱ vahni̱r āta̍no̱t sīvya̱n tamā̍ṁsi̱ dudhi̍tā̱ sam a̍vyayat ||
english: Then he who surpassed all worlds in greatness, the sovereign maker with his swift-flying power, grew great. Forthwith the carrier extended both worlds with light, sewing up the darkness he wrapped it fast.

sanskrit: sa prā̱cīnā̱n parva̍tān dṛṁha̱d oja̍sādharā̱cīna̍m akṛṇod a̱pām apa̍ḥ | adhā̍rayat pṛthi̱vīṁ vi̱śvadhā̍yasa̱m asta̍bhnān mā̱yayā̱ dyām a̍va̱srasa̍ḥ ||
english: He strengthened the eastern mountains with his might, he made the waters flow downward. He held up the earth that nourishes all; by his magic power he propped up the sky lest it fall.

sanskrit: sāsmā̱ ara̍m bā̱hubhyā̱ṁ yam pi̱tākṛ̍ṇo̱d viśva̍smā̱d ā ja̱nuṣo̱ veda̍sa̱s pari̍ | yenā̍ pṛthi̱vyāṁ ni krivi̍ṁ śa̱yadhyai̱ vajre̍ṇa ha̱tvy avṛ̍ṇak tuvi̱ṣvaṇi̍ḥ ||
english: The weapon which the father made ready for him with both arms, choosing it from all beings and all birth — with that thunderbolt, having struck, the loud-sounding one opened the way to lay Kṛvi low upon the earth.

sanskrit: a̱mā̱jūr i̍va pi̱troḥ sacā̍ sa̱tī sa̍mā̱nād ā sada̍sa̱s tvām i̍ye̱ bhaga̍m | kṛ̱dhi pra̍ke̱tam upa̍ mā̱sy ā bha̍ra da̱ddhi bhā̱gaṁ ta̱nvo̱3̱̍ yena̍ mā̱maha̍ḥ ||
english: Like an old maid staying at home with her parents, I seek blessing from thee from the common seat. Make me conspicuous, bring to me — give the bodily share by which thou wouldst magnify.

sanskrit: bho̱jaṁ tvām i̍ndra va̱yaṁ hu̍vema da̱diṣ ṭvam i̱ndrāpā̍ṁsi̱ vājā̍n | a̱vi̱ḍḍhī̍ndra ci̱trayā̍ na ū̱tī kṛ̱dhi vṛ̍ṣann indra̱ vasya̍so naḥ ||
english: As the bountiful one we call thee, O Indra — do thou give, Indra, drinks and prizes. Guard us, Indra, with splendid aid; make us richer, O bull Indra.

sanskrit: nū̱naṁ sā te̱ prati̱ vara̍ṁ jari̱tre du̍hī̱yad i̍ndra̱ dakṣi̍ṇā ma̱ghonī̍ | śikṣā̍ sto̱tṛbhyo̱ māti̍ dha̱g bhago̍ no bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: Now may that generous dakshinā of thine, O Indra, yield to the singer in return for his choice. Be bountiful to the praisers; let not our fortune be consumed — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.

sanskrit: prā̱tā ratho̱ navo̍ yoji̱ sasni̱ś catu̍ryugas trika̱śaḥ sa̱ptara̍śmiḥ | daśā̍ritro manu̱ṣya̍ḥ sva̱rṣāḥ sa i̱ṣṭibhi̍r ma̱tibhī̱ raṁhyo̍ bhūt ||
english: At dawn a new winning chariot was yoked, four-horsed, three-whipped, seven-reined, ten-oared — a human one winning the sun; may it be swift by sacrificial rites and prayers.

sanskrit: sāsmā̱ ara̍m pratha̱maṁ sa dvi̱tīya̍m u̱to tṛ̱tīya̱m manu̍ṣa̱ḥ sa hotā̍ | a̱nyasyā̱ garbha̍m a̱nya ū̍ jananta̱ so a̱nyebhi̍ḥ sacate̱ jenyo̱ vṛṣā̍ ||
english: He was prepared first, the second and the third — the human priest. One is born from another's womb; another begets; he, the conquering bull, accompanies still others.

sanskrit: harī̱ nu ka̱ṁ ratha̱ indra̍sya yojam ā̱yai sū̱ktena̱ vaca̍sā̱ nave̍na | mo ṣu tvām atra̍ ba̱havo̱ hi viprā̱ ni rī̍rama̱n yaja̍mānāso a̱nye ||
english: Now with a fresh well-spoken word let me yoke the two bay horses to Indra's chariot to come here. May not the many seers detain thee here, nor other sacrificers.

sanskrit: ā dvābhyā̱ṁ hari̍bhyām indra yā̱hy ā ca̱turbhi̱r ā ṣa̱ḍbhir hū̱yamā̍naḥ | āṣṭā̱bhir da̱śabhi̍ḥ soma̱peya̍m a̱yaṁ su̱taḥ su̍makha̱ mā mṛdha̍s kaḥ ||
english: Come, Indra, with thy two bay horses; come with four, come with six, being invoked. Come with eight, with ten — this soma has been pressed for drinking; O fair-faced one, do not despise it.

sanskrit: ā vi̍ṁśa̱tyā tri̱ṁśatā̍ yāhy a̱rvāṅ ā ca̍tvāri̱ṁśatā̱ hari̍bhir yujā̱naḥ | ā pa̍ñcā̱śatā̍ su̱rathe̍bhir i̱ndrā ṣa̱ṣṭyā sa̍pta̱tyā so̍ma̱peya̍m ||
english: Come hither with twenty, with thirty; come yoked with forty bay horses. Come, Indra, with fifty well-horsed ones, with sixty, with seventy — here is soma for drinking.

sanskrit: āśī̱tyā na̍va̱tyā yā̍hy a̱rvāṅ ā śa̱tena̱ hari̍bhir u̱hyamā̍naḥ | a̱yaṁ hi te̍ śu̱naho̍treṣu̱ soma̱ indra̍ tvā̱yā pari̍ṣikto̱ madā̍ya ||
english: Come hither with eighty, with ninety; come carried by a hundred bay horses. For this soma in the Śunahtra rites, O Indra, has been poured out for thine own exhilaration.

sanskrit: mama̱ brahme̍ndra yā̱hy acchā̱ viśvā̱ harī̍ dhu̱ri dhi̍ṣvā̱ ratha̍sya | pu̱ru̱trā hi vi̱havyo̍ ba̱bhūthā̱smiñ chū̍ra̱ sava̍ne mādayasva ||
english: Come toward my prayer, Indra; place all thy bay horses on the yoke of thy chariot. For thou hast been invocable in many places — at this pressing, O hero, be exhilarated.

sanskrit: na ma̱ indre̍ṇa sa̱khyaṁ vi yo̍ṣad a̱smabhya̍m asya̱ dakṣi̍ṇā duhīta | upa̱ jyeṣṭhe̱ varū̍the̱ gabha̍stau prā̱ye-prā̍ye jigī̱vāṁsa̍ḥ syāma ||
english: May friendship with Indra not depart from me; may his right-hand gift yield to us. Under his highest shelter, under his arm, may we be victorious at each and every contest.

sanskrit: nū̱naṁ sā te̱ prati̱ vara̍ṁ jari̱tre du̍hī̱yad i̍ndra̱ dakṣi̍ṇā ma̱ghonī̍ | śikṣā̍ sto̱tṛbhyo̱ māti̍ dha̱g bhago̍ no bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: Now may that generous dakshinā of thine, O Indra, yield to the singer in return for his choice. Be bountiful to the praisers; let not our fortune be consumed — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.

sanskrit: apā̍yy a̱syāndha̍so̱ madā̍ya̱ manī̍ṣiṇaḥ suvā̱nasya̱ praya̍saḥ | yasmi̱nn indra̍ḥ pra̱divi̍ vāvṛdhā̱na oko̍ da̱dhe bra̍hma̱ṇyanta̍ś ca̱ nara̍ḥ ||
english: Drunk for the rapture of this soma draught, of the pressed offering of the wise men — in whom Indra, waxing great since ancient times, has set his abode, and in whom men delight in prayer.

sanskrit: a̱sya ma̍ndā̱no madhvo̱ vajra̍ha̱sto 'hi̱m indro̍ arṇo̱vṛta̱ṁ vi vṛ̍ścat | pra yad vayo̱ na svasa̍rā̱ṇy acchā̱ prayā̍ṁsi ca na̱dīnā̱ṁ cakra̍manta ||
english: Exhilarated by this sweet honey, thunderbolt in hand, Indra cut through the serpent that had dammed the waters, when the streams advanced toward their own resting places and the offerings of the rivers moved forward.

sanskrit: sa māhi̍na̱ indro̱ arṇo̍ a̱pām praira̍yad ahi̱hācchā̍ samu̱dram | aja̍naya̱t sūrya̍ṁ vi̱dad gā a̱ktunāhnā̍ṁ va̱yunā̍ni sādhat ||
english: That great Indra drove the flood of the waters toward the ocean, slaying the serpent. He begat the sun, he found the cows; with night-light he established the courses of the days.

sanskrit: so a̍pra̱tīni̱ mana̍ve pu̱rūṇīndro̍ dāśad dā̱śuṣe̱ hanti̍ vṛ̱tram | sa̱dyo yo nṛbhyo̍ ata̱sāyyo̱ bhūt pa̍spṛdhā̱nebhya̱ḥ sūrya̍sya sā̱tau ||
english: He gave many unresisted gifts to Manu, the worshipper; Indra smites Vṛtra. He who at once became unconquerable for men in the contest for the sun.

sanskrit: sa su̍nva̱ta indra̱ḥ sūrya̱m ā de̱vo ri̍ṇa̱ṅ martyā̍ya sta̱vān | ā yad ra̱yiṁ gu̱had adā̍dyam asmai̱ bhara̱d aṁśa̱ṁ naita̍śo daśa̱syan ||
english: Indra, being praised, released the sun for the mortal, the presser; when he brought forth the hidden treasure not given away, when Naitaśa brought him his share, willing.

sanskrit: sa ra̍ndhayat sa̱diva̱ḥ sāra̍thaye̱ śuṣṇa̍m a̱śuṣa̱ṁ kuya̍va̱ṁ kutsā̍ya | divo̍dāsāya nava̱tiṁ ca̱ navendra̱ḥ puro̱ vy ai̍ra̱c chamba̍rasya ||
english: He ever made Śuṣṇa, the shriveller, yield to his charioteer, the evil Kuyava to Kutsa. Indra smashed the ninety and nine strongholds of Śambara for Divo-dāsa.

sanskrit: e̱vā ta̍ indro̱catha̍m ahema śrava̱syā na tmanā̍ vā̱jaya̍ntaḥ | a̱śyāma̱ tat sāpta̍m āśuṣā̱ṇā na̱namo̱ vadha̱r ade̍vasya pī̱yoḥ ||
english: Thus may we proclaim for thee, Indra, the praise, seeking renown, spurring ourselves on our own. May we attain that sevenfold prize, pressing eagerly; we bow down to the weapon slaying the ungodly one who mocks.

sanskrit: e̱vā te̍ gṛtsama̱dāḥ śū̍ra̱ manmā̍va̱syavo̱ na va̱yunā̍ni takṣuḥ | bra̱hma̱ṇyanta̍ indra te̱ navī̍ya̱ iṣa̱m ūrja̍ṁ sukṣi̱tiṁ su̱mnam a̍śyuḥ ||
english: Thus the Gṛtsamadas, O hero, seeking shelter, have fashioned prayer for thee like guides. Delighting in prayer, Indra, they who sing thy newer hymn shall win food, strength, good dwelling, and happiness.

sanskrit: nū̱naṁ sā te̱ prati̱ vara̍ṁ jari̱tre du̍hī̱yad i̍ndra̱ dakṣi̍ṇā ma̱ghonī̍ | śikṣā̍ sto̱tṛbhyo̱ māti̍ dha̱g bhago̍ no bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: Now may that generous dakshinā of thine, O Indra, yield to the singer in return for his choice. Be bountiful to the praisers; let not our fortune be consumed — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.

sanskrit: va̱yaṁ te̱ vaya̍ indra vi̱ddhi ṣu ṇa̱ḥ pra bha̍rāmahe vāja̱yur na ratha̍m | vi̱pa̱nyavo̱ dīdhya̍to manī̱ṣā su̱mnam iya̍kṣanta̱s tvāva̍to̱ nṝn ||
english: We are thy offspring, Indra — know us indeed; we drive forth eagerly like a chariot seeking the prize. Wise ones meditating with prayer, seeking the grace of thee and of thy men.

sanskrit: tvaṁ na̍ indra̱ tvābhi̍r ū̱tī tvā̍ya̱to a̍bhiṣṭi̱pāsi̱ janā̍n | tvam i̱no dā̱śuṣo̍ varū̱tetthādhī̍r a̱bhi yo nakṣa̍ti tvā ||
english: Thou, Indra, with thine own aids guardest the peoples devoted to thee as their protector. Thou art the lord and shelter of the worshipper — thus planning, him who approaches thee.

sanskrit: sa no̱ yuvendro̍ jo̱hūtra̱ḥ sakhā̍ śi̱vo na̱rām a̍stu pā̱tā | yaḥ śaṁsa̍nta̱ṁ yaḥ śa̍śamā̱nam ū̱tī paca̍ntaṁ ca stu̱vanta̍ṁ ca pra̱ṇeṣa̍t ||
english: May young Indra, much invoked, be to us a friendly comrade, a protector of men — he who guides with his aid the one reciting and the one who has laboured, the one cooking and the one praising.

sanskrit: tam u̍ stuṣa̱ indra̱ṁ taṁ gṛ̍ṇīṣe̱ yasmi̍n pu̱rā vā̍vṛ̱dhuḥ śā̍śa̱duś ca̍ | sa vasva̱ḥ kāma̍m pīparad iyā̱no bra̍hmaṇya̱to nūta̍nasyā̱yoḥ ||
english: That Indra do I praise, that one do I invoke, in whom in the past men waxed strong and prospered. He shall satisfy the desire for wealth as he advances, of the one delighting in prayer, of the new generation.

sanskrit: so aṅgi̍rasām u̱cathā̍ juju̱ṣvān brahmā̍ tūto̱d indro̍ gā̱tum i̱ṣṇan | mu̱ṣṇann u̱ṣasa̱ḥ sūrye̍ṇa sta̱vān aśna̍sya cic chiśnathat pū̱rvyāṇi̍ ||
english: Delighting in the praises of the Aṅgirases, Indra the inspired poet drove on, spurring the way. Wresting away the dawns with the sun, when praised, he clove asunder the ancient things of the rock.

sanskrit: sa ha̍ śru̱ta indro̱ nāma̍ de̱va ū̱rdhvo bhu̍va̱n manu̍ṣe da̱smata̍maḥ | ava̍ pri̱yam a̍rśasā̱nasya̍ sā̱hvāñ chiro̍ bharad dā̱sasya̍ sva̱dhāvā̍n ||
english: Verily famed is the god Indra by name; he became the highest, most marvellous for man. Having challenged the favourite of the one reigning, the self-powerful one bore off the head of the Dāsa.

sanskrit: sa vṛ̍tra̱hendra̍ḥ kṛ̱ṣṇayo̍nīḥ puraṁda̱ro dāsī̍r airaya̱d vi | aja̍naya̱t mana̍ve̱ kṣām a̱paś ca̍ sa̱trā śaṁsa̱ṁ yaja̍mānasya tūtot ||
english: That Vṛtra-slaying Indra, breaker of strongholds, drove away the dark-wombed Dāsa women. He generated earth and waters for Manu; he altogether spurred on the glory of the sacrificer.

sanskrit: tasmai̍ tava̱sya1̱̍m anu̍ dāyi sa̱trendrā̍ya de̱vebhi̱r arṇa̍sātau | prati̱ yad a̍sya̱ vajra̍m bā̱hvor dhur ha̱tvī dasyū̱n pura̱ āya̍sī̱r ni tā̍rīt ||
english: For that powerful Indra a gift was assigned by the gods in the battle of the flood, when he placed the thunderbolt on his two arms and, having slain the Dasyus, he drove through the iron fortresses.

sanskrit: nū̱naṁ sā te̱ prati̱ vara̍ṁ jari̱tre du̍hī̱yad i̍ndra̱ dakṣi̍ṇā ma̱ghonī̍ | śikṣā̍ sto̱tṛbhyo̱ māti̍ dha̱g bhago̍ no bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: Now may that generous dakshinā of thine, O Indra, yield to the singer in return for his choice. Be bountiful to the praisers; let not our fortune be consumed — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.

sanskrit: vi̱śva̱jite̍ dhana̱jite̍ sva̱rjite̍ satrā̱jite̍ nṛ̱jita̍ urvarā̱jite̍ | a̱śva̱jite̍ go̱jite̍ a̱bjite̍ bha̱rendrā̍ya̱ soma̍ṁ yaja̱tāya̍ harya̱tam ||
english: Bring soma, dear to the adorable Indra — to the all-conqueror, the wealth-conqueror, the sky-conqueror, the all-vanquisher, the man-conqueror, the field-conqueror, the horse-conqueror, the cow-conqueror, the water-conqueror.

sanskrit: a̱bhi̱bhuve̍ 'bhibha̱ṅgāya̍ vanva̱te 'ṣā̍ḻhāya̱ saha̍mānāya ve̱dhase̍ | tu̱vi̱graye̱ vahna̍ye du̱ṣṭarī̍tave satrā̱sāhe̱ nama̱ indrā̍ya vocata ||
english: Proclaim homage to Indra — to the overwhelming, the utterly crushing, the desiring, the unconquerable, the enduring, the ordaining, the strongly assailing, the propelling, the hard to check, the all-overpowering.

sanskrit: sa̱trā̱sā̱ho ja̍nabha̱kṣo ja̍naṁsa̱haś cyava̍no yu̱dhmo anu̱ joṣa̍m ukṣi̱taḥ | vṛ̱ta̱ṁca̱yaḥ sahu̍rir vi̱kṣv ā̍ri̱ta indra̍sya voca̱m pra kṛ̱tāni̍ vī̱ryā̍ ||
english: All-overpowering, people-devouring, people-subduing, the warrior Indra who shakes, sprinkled according to his pleasure, the obstructor-slayer, the subduer, who is invoked among the peoples — may I proclaim the heroic deeds Indra has performed.

sanskrit: a̱nā̱nu̱do vṛ̍ṣa̱bho dodha̍to va̱dho ga̍mbhī̱ra ṛ̱ṣvo asa̍maṣṭakāvyaḥ | ra̱dhra̱co̱daḥ śnatha̍no vīḻi̱tas pṛ̱thur indra̍ḥ suya̱jña u̱ṣasa̱ḥ sva̍r janat ||
english: Irresistible bull, the quaking death-stroke, deep, noble, of incomparable poetic skill, driving the helpless ones, destroying, firm and broad — Indra, worshipped well, generated the dawns and the sun.

sanskrit: ya̱jñena̍ gā̱tum a̱pturo̍ vividrire̱ dhiyo̍ hinvā̱nā u̱śijo̍ manī̱ṣiṇa̍ḥ | a̱bhi̱svarā̍ ni̱ṣadā̱ gā a̍va̱syava̱ indre̍ hinvā̱nā dravi̍ṇāny āśata ||
english: By sacrifice the skilful ones found the way; the Uśijas, wise ones, spurring forward with prayers, sitting around the cows that echo with chants, seeking protection, spurring Indra, they attained riches.

sanskrit: indra̱ śreṣṭhā̍ni̱ dravi̍ṇāni dhehi̱ citti̱ṁ dakṣa̍sya subhaga̱tvam a̱sme | poṣa̍ṁ rayī̱ṇām ari̍ṣṭiṁ ta̱nūnā̍ṁ svā̱dmāna̍ṁ vā̱caḥ su̍dina̱tvam ahnā̍m ||
english: O Indra, bestow the best of riches upon us; the wisdom of skill and good fortune for us. The increase of wealth, the uninjured state of our bodies, the good taste of speech, and the auspiciousness of our days.

sanskrit: trika̍drukeṣu mahi̱ṣo yavā̍śiraṁ tuvi̱śuṣma̍s tṛ̱pat soma̍m apiba̱d viṣṇu̍nā su̱taṁ yathāva̍śat | sa ī̍m mamāda̱ mahi̱ karma̱ karta̍ve ma̱hām u̱ruṁ saina̍ṁ saścad de̱vo de̱vaṁ sa̱tyam indra̍ṁ sa̱tya indu̍ḥ ||
english: The great bull was satisfied and drank at the three Trikadrukas the soma mixed with barley, pressed by Viṣṇu, as he willed — the mighty one was exhilarated to do the great deed. The great, far-reaching drop follows the true god, Indra, the true god.

sanskrit: adha̱ tviṣī̍mām̐ a̱bhy oja̍sā̱ krivi̍ṁ yu̱dhābha̍va̱d ā roda̍sī apṛṇad asya ma̱jmanā̱ pra vā̍vṛdhe | adha̍ttā̱nyaṁ ja̱ṭhare̱ prem a̍ricyata̱ saina̍ṁ saścad de̱vo de̱vaṁ sa̱tyam indra̍ṁ sa̱tya indu̍ḥ ||
english: Then, radiant, in battle he attacked Kṛvi with his might; he filled the two world-halves; by his greatness he increased. Then he placed another in his belly, and overflowed from it — the true drop follows the true god Indra, the true god.

sanskrit: sā̱kaṁ jā̱taḥ kratu̍nā sā̱kam oja̍sā vavakṣitha sā̱kaṁ vṛ̱ddho vī̱ryai̍ḥ sāsa̱hir mṛdho̱ vica̍rṣaṇiḥ | dātā̱ rādha̍ḥ stuva̱te kāmya̱ṁ vasu̱ saina̍ṁ saścad de̱vo de̱vaṁ sa̱tyam indra̍ṁ sa̱tya indu̍ḥ ||
english: Born at once with will-power, thou hast grown together with strength; grown great at once with heroic deeds, the overwhelmer of enemies, the all-seeing. The giver of desirable wealth to the praiser — the true drop follows the true god Indra, the true god.

sanskrit: tava̱ tyan narya̍ṁ nṛ̱to 'pa̍ indra pratha̱mam pū̱rvyaṁ di̱vi pra̱vācya̍ṁ kṛ̱tam | yad de̱vasya̱ śava̍sā̱ prāri̍ṇā̱ asu̍ṁ ri̱ṇann a̱paḥ | bhuva̱d viśva̍m a̱bhy āde̍va̱m oja̍sā vi̱dād ūrja̍ṁ śa̱takra̍tur vi̱dād iṣa̍m ||
english: That manly deed of thine, O dancer Indra, the first, primeval, proclaimed in heaven — when by the god's might thou didst let loose the vital breath, releasing the waters; all the ungodly one became subject through thy might; the hundred-minded one found strength, found refreshment.

sanskrit: ga̱ṇānā̍ṁ tvā ga̱ṇapa̍tiṁ havāmahe ka̱viṁ ka̍vī̱nām u̍pa̱maśra̍vastamam | jye̱ṣṭha̱rāja̱m brahma̍ṇām brahmaṇas pata̱ ā na̍ḥ śṛ̱ṇvann ū̱tibhi̍ḥ sīda̱ sāda̍nam ||
english: We call thee, lord of the troops, Gaṇapati, the poet among poets, most widely famed — king supreme of prayers, O Brahmaṇaspati; hearing us, come, take thy seat with thine aids in the seat of worship.

sanskrit: de̱vāś ci̍t te asurya̱ prace̍taso̱ bṛha̍spate ya̱jñiya̍m bhā̱gam ā̍naśuḥ | u̱srā i̍va̱ sūryo̱ jyoti̍ṣā ma̱ho viśve̍ṣā̱m ij ja̍ni̱tā brahma̍ṇām asi ||
english: Even the gods, O Bṛhaspati, thy far-seeing lordly ones, obtained their sacrificial share. Like mornings by the sun's great light — thou art verily the progenitor of all sacred formulas.

sanskrit: ā vi̱bādhyā̍ pari̱rāpa̱s tamā̍ṁsi ca̱ jyoti̍ṣmanta̱ṁ ratha̍m ṛ̱tasya̍ tiṣṭhasi | bṛha̍spate bhī̱mam a̍mitra̱dambha̍naṁ rakṣo̱haṇa̍ṁ gotra̱bhida̍ṁ sva̱rvida̍m ||
english: Driving away the slanderers and the dark ones, thou standest on the luminous chariot of cosmic order, O Bṛhaspati — terrible, crushing the enemies, slaying the Rākṣasas, cleaving the mountain cave, finding the sun.

sanskrit: su̱nī̱tibhi̍r nayasi̱ trāya̍se̱ jana̱ṁ yas tubhya̱ṁ dāśā̱n na tam aṁho̍ aśnavat | bra̱hma̱dviṣa̱s tapa̍no manyu̱mīr a̍si̱ bṛha̍spate̱ mahi̱ tat te̍ mahitva̱nam ||
english: With good guidance thou leadest and protectest the man who has offered to thee; no distress overtakes him. Thou art the scorcher of those who hate sacred prayer, the source of wrath, O Bṛhaspati — great is that thy greatness.

sanskrit: na tam aṁho̱ na du̍ri̱taṁ kuta̍ś ca̱na nārā̍tayas titiru̱r na dva̍yā̱vina̍ḥ | viśvā̱ id a̍smād dhva̱raso̱ vi bā̍dhase̱ yaṁ su̍go̱pā rakṣa̍si brahmaṇas pate ||
english: No distress, no mishap from anywhere overwhelms him, nor do enmities, nor the deceitful — all crookedness thou drivest away from him whom thou, well-protecting, guardest, O Brahmaṇaspati.

sanskrit: tvaṁ no̍ go̱pāḥ pa̍thi̱kṛd vi̍cakṣa̱ṇas tava̍ vra̱tāya̍ ma̱tibhi̍r jarāmahe | bṛha̍spate̱ yo no̍ a̱bhi hvaro̍ da̱dhe svā tam ma̍rmartu du̱cchunā̱ hara̍svatī ||
english: Thou art our guardian, path-maker, far-seeing; by our prayers we worship according to thy ordinance. O Bṛhaspati, whoever places crooked intent against us — may calamity, the hateful one, afflict that man himself.

sanskrit: u̱ta vā̱ yo no̍ ma̱rcayā̱d anā̍gaso 'rātī̱vā marta̍ḥ sānu̱ko vṛka̍ḥ | bṛha̍spate̱ apa̱ taṁ va̍rtayā pa̱thaḥ su̱gaṁ no̍ a̱syai de̱vavī̍taye kṛdhi ||
english: Or whosoever would harm us, though we are guiltless — a mortal, like an enemy wolf who sneaks close — O Bṛhaspati, turn him from the path; make it easy for us on this path to the divine gathering.

sanskrit: trā̱tāra̍ṁ tvā ta̱nūnā̍ṁ havāma̱he 'va̍spartar adhiva̱ktāra̍m asma̱yum ||  | bṛha̍spate deva̱nido̱ ni ba̍rhaya̱ mā du̱revā̱ utta̍raṁ su̱mnam un na̍śan ||
english: We call thee as protector of our bodies, as the rescuer, the advocate, who favours us. O Bṛhaspati, crush down the revilers of the gods; may the ill-intentioned not attain the highest happiness.

sanskrit: tvayā̍ va̱yaṁ su̱vṛdhā̍ brahmaṇas pate spā̱rhā vasu̍ manu̱ṣyā da̍dīmahi | yā no̍ dū̱re ta̱ḻito̱ yā arā̍tayo̱ 'bhi santi̍ ja̱mbhayā̱ tā a̍na̱pnasa̍ḥ ||
english: With thee, O Brahmaṇaspati, who makest well grow, may we receive the desirable, human good things. The enmities that are afar, the thunderings against us, the hostilities that threaten us — crush them all, the harmless ones.

sanskrit: tvayā̍ va̱yam u̍tta̱maṁ dhī̍mahe̱ vayo̱ bṛha̍spate̱ papri̍ṇā̱ sasni̍nā yu̱jā | mā no̍ du̱ḥśaṁso̍ abhidi̱psur ī̍śata̱ pra su̱śaṁsā̍ ma̱tibhi̍s tāriṣīmahi ||
english: With thee, O Bṛhaspati, the filling companion who conquers, may we attain the highest wellbeing. Let not the ill-spoken one who desires to harm us rule us; may we overcome with prayers, well-spoken.

sanskrit: a̱nā̱nu̱do vṛ̍ṣa̱bho jagmi̍r āha̱vaṁ niṣṭa̍ptā̱ śatru̱m pṛta̍nāsu sāsa̱hiḥ | asi̍ sa̱tya ṛ̍ṇa̱yā bra̍hmaṇas pata u̱grasya̍ cid dami̱tā vī̍ḻuha̱rṣiṇa̍ḥ ||
english: Irresistible bull, going to the invocation, who burns down the enemy, who has conquered in battles — thou art the truly due debt-exactor, O Brahmaṇaspati, the tamer even of the violent and bold-rejoicing one.

sanskrit: ade̍vena̱ mana̍sā̱ yo ri̍ṣa̱ṇyati̍ śā̱sām u̱gro manya̍māno̱ jighā̍ṁsati | bṛha̍spate̱ mā praṇa̱k tasya̍ no va̱dho ni ka̍rma ma̱nyuṁ du̱reva̍sya̱ śardha̍taḥ ||
english: He who intends to harm with ungodly mind, who powerful and imperious seeks to slay — O Bṛhaspati, let not his deadly blow reach us; lay down the wrath of the evilly-abiding proud one.

sanskrit: bhare̍ṣu̱ havyo̱ nama̍sopa̱sadyo̱ gantā̱ vāje̍ṣu̱ sani̍tā̱ dhana̍ṁ-dhanam | viśvā̱ id a̱ryo a̍bhidi̱psvo̱3̱̍ mṛdho̱ bṛha̱spati̱r vi va̍varhā̱ rathā̍m̐ iva ||
english: He is to be called upon in battles, to be approached with reverence, the one who goes to the prizes and wins wealth upon wealth. All the attacks of the enemy who desires to harm, Bṛhaspati has driven away like chariots.

sanskrit: teji̍ṣṭhayā tapa̱nī ra̱kṣasa̍s tapa̱ ye tvā̍ ni̱de da̍dhi̱re dṛ̱ṣṭavī̍ryam | ā̱vis tat kṛ̍ṣva̱ yad asa̍t ta u̱kthya1̱̍m bṛha̍spate̱ vi pa̍ri̱rāpo̍ ardaya ||
english: With the most keen and scorching one, scorch the Rākṣasas who have held thee in contempt, whose powers are manifest. Make that praiseworthy thing visible which is to be; O Bṛhaspati, afflict and crush the slanderers.

sanskrit: bṛha̍spate̱ ati̱ yad a̱ryo arhā̍d dyu̱mad vi̱bhāti̱ kratu̍ma̱j jane̍ṣu | yad dī̱daya̱c chava̍sa ṛtaprajāta̱ tad a̱smāsu̱ dravi̍ṇaṁ dhehi ci̱tram ||
english: O Bṛhaspati, that which surpasses the stranger's excellence, which shines luminously with wisdom among the peoples — that which blazes with power, O thou born of ṛta — bestow that brilliant wealth upon us.

sanskrit: mā na̍ḥ ste̱nebhyo̱ ye a̱bhi dru̱has pa̱de ni̍rā̱miṇo̍ ri̱pavo̱ 'nne̍ṣu jāgṛ̱dhuḥ | ā de̱vānā̱m oha̍te̱ vi vrayo̍ hṛ̱di bṛha̍spate̱ na pa̱raḥ sāmno̍ viduḥ ||
english: O Bṛhaspati, let not thieves, those who would injure, the destructive enemies who lie in wait for prey, be against us. At the summons of the gods the woollen threads are spread upon the heart — no one beyond knows the secret.

sanskrit: viśve̍bhyo̱ hi tvā̱ bhuva̍nebhya̱s pari̱ tvaṣṭāja̍na̱t sāmna̍ḥ-sāmnaḥ ka̱viḥ ||  | sa ṛ̍ṇa̱cid ṛ̍ṇa̱yā brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̍r dru̱ho ha̱ntā ma̱ha ṛ̱tasya̍ dha̱rtari̍ ||
english: Tvaṣṭṛ created thee, the poet, beyond all worlds, sāman by sāman. He, the debt-exactor, the exactor of debts, is Brahmaṇaspati, the slayer of wrong, the upholder of great cosmic order.

sanskrit: tava̍ śri̱ye vy a̍jihīta̱ parva̍to̱ gavā̍ṁ go̱tram u̱dasṛ̍jo̱ yad a̍ṅgiraḥ | indre̍ṇa yu̱jā tama̍sā̱ parī̍vṛta̱m bṛha̍spate̱ nir a̱pām au̍bjo arṇa̱vam ||
english: For thy glory the mountain opened wide when the cave of the cows was unsealed, O Aṅgiras. Allied with Indra, O Bṛhaspati, thou didst cause the ocean of the waters, surrounded by darkness, to stream forth.

sanskrit: brahma̍ṇas pate̱ tvam a̱sya ya̱ntā sū̱ktasya̍ bodhi̱ tana̍yaṁ ca jinva | viśva̱ṁ tad bha̱draṁ yad ava̍nti de̱vā bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: O Brahmaṇaspati, be thou the controller of this hymn; be aware, and quicken its offspring. All that is blessed which the gods protect — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.

sanskrit: semām a̍viḍḍhi̱ prabhṛ̍ti̱ṁ ya īśi̍ṣe̱ 'yā vi̍dhema̱ nava̍yā ma̱hā gi̱rā | yathā̍ no mī̱ḍhvān stava̍te̱ sakhā̱ tava̱ bṛha̍spate̱ sīṣa̍dha̱ḥ sota no̍ ma̱tim ||
english: Protect this offering here, thou who art lord; with this fresh great hymn we would worship. So that the bounteous one, thy friend, praises us, O Bṛhaspati, succeed and quicken our prayer.

sanskrit: yo nantvā̱ny ana̍ma̱n ny oja̍so̱tāda̍rdar ma̱nyunā̱ śamba̍rāṇi̱ vi | prācyā̍vaya̱d acyu̍tā̱ brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̱r ā cāvi̍śa̱d vasu̍manta̱ṁ vi parva̍tam ||
english: He who bent the bending obstacles down with his might, and shattered the devices of Śambara with wrath — Brahmaṇaspati set shaking what was immovable and entered and opened the wealth-containing mountain.

sanskrit: tad de̱vānā̍ṁ de̱vata̍māya̱ kartva̱m aśra̍thnan dṛ̱ḻhāvra̍danta vīḻi̱tā | ud gā ā̍ja̱d abhi̍na̱d brahma̍ṇā va̱lam agū̍ha̱t tamo̱ vy a̍cakṣaya̱t sva̍ḥ ||
english: That was to be done for the most divine of the gods — the firm ones unloosed and broke apart the solid strongholds. He drove the cows out; with his prayer he clove Vala; he hid the darkness and made the sunlight visible.

sanskrit: aśmā̍syam ava̱tam brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̱r madhu̍dhāram a̱bhi yam oja̱sātṛ̍ṇat | tam e̱va viśve̍ papire sva̱rdṛśo̍ ba̱hu sā̱kaṁ si̍sicu̱r utsa̍m u̱driṇa̍m ||
english: Brahmaṇaspati pierced with his might the rocky cave that streams with honey. All those who see the sun drank from that very one; together they poured into the welling spring abundantly.

sanskrit: sanā̱ tā kā ci̱d bhuva̍nā̱ bhavī̍tvā mā̱dbhiḥ śa̱radbhi̱r duro̍ varanta vaḥ | aya̍tantā carato a̱nyad-a̍nya̱d id yā ca̱kāra̍ va̱yunā̱ brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̍ḥ ||
english: Whatever worlds there are that have been and are yet to be — for many seasons their doors have been closed to you. Roaming without effort, each in a different direction, are the courses that Brahmaṇaspati has ordained.

sanskrit: a̱bhi̱nakṣa̍nto a̱bhi ye tam ā̍na̱śur ni̱dhim pa̍ṇī̱nām pa̍ra̱maṁ guhā̍ hi̱tam | te vi̱dvāṁsa̍ḥ prati̱cakṣyānṛ̍tā̱ puna̱r yata̍ u̱ āya̱n tad ud ī̍yur ā̱viśa̍m ||
english: Those who approached and attained to it, the supreme treasure of the Paṇis, hidden in the cave — those wise ones, looking back at the untruth, from whence they had come, rose up openly.

sanskrit: ṛ̱tāvā̍naḥ prati̱cakṣyānṛ̍tā̱ puna̱r āta̱ ā ta̍sthuḥ ka̱vayo̍ ma̱has pa̱thaḥ | te bā̱hubhyā̍ṁ dhami̱tam a̱gnim aśma̍ni̱ naki̱ḥ ṣo a̱sty ara̍ṇo ja̱hur hi tam ||
english: Those who possess cosmic order, looking back at untruth, came and stood firm on the path of the great. They by both arms fanned the fire in the stone — there is none who is a stranger; verily they abandoned him.

sanskrit: ṛ̱tajye̍na kṣi̱preṇa̱ brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̱r yatra̱ vaṣṭi̱ pra tad a̍śnoti̱ dhanva̍nā | tasya̍ sā̱dhvīr iṣa̍vo̱ yābhi̱r asya̍ti nṛ̱cakṣa̍so dṛ̱śaye̱ karṇa̍yonayaḥ ||
english: Brahmaṇaspati with the bow-string of cosmic order, with the swift one — where he desires, thither he reaches with his bow. His are the true arrows with which he shoots, for seeing by men; those born for the ear.

sanskrit: sa sa̍ṁna̱yaḥ sa vi̍na̱yaḥ pu̱rohi̍ta̱ḥ sa suṣṭu̍ta̱ḥ sa yu̱dhi brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̍ḥ | cā̱kṣmo yad vāja̱m bhara̍te ma̱tī dhanād it sūrya̍s tapati tapya̱tur vṛthā̍ ||
english: He is the leader, the guide, the domestic priest, the one well praised, the warrior — Brahmaṇaspati. He is fit to see when prayer brings the prize; it is from wealth alone that the sun burns; the heat burns in vain.

sanskrit: vi̱bhu pra̱bhu pra̍tha̱mam me̱hanā̍vato̱ bṛha̱spate̍ḥ suvi̱datrā̍ṇi̱ rādhyā̍ | i̱mā sā̱tāni̍ ve̱nyasya̍ vā̱jino̱ yena̱ janā̍ u̱bhaye̍ bhuñja̱te viśa̍ḥ ||
english: Vast, mighty, the first — of the exuberant Bṛhaspati the riches to be attained are well-known. These prizes of the admirable prize-winner — with which both peoples enjoy, the clans.

sanskrit: yo 'va̍re vṛ̱jane̍ vi̱śvathā̍ vi̱bhur ma̱hām u̍ ra̱ṇvaḥ śava̍sā va̱vakṣi̍tha | sa de̱vo de̱vān prati̍ paprathe pṛ̱thu viśved u̱ tā pa̍ri̱bhūr brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̍ḥ ||
english: He who is all-pervading in the lower assembly and great — joyful, grown great by power. That god extended wide before the gods; Brahmaṇaspati is the encompasser of all these things.

sanskrit: viśva̍ṁ sa̱tyam ma̍ghavānā yu̱vor id āpa̍ś ca̱na pra mi̍nanti vra̱taṁ vā̍m | acche̍ndrābrahmaṇaspatī ha̱vir no 'nna̱ṁ yuje̍va vā̱jinā̍ jigātam ||
english: All truth is yours indeed, O bounteous pair; even the waters do not transgress your ordinance. Come to our oblation, O Indra and Brahmaṇaspati — come to our food like two prize-winners to a yoke.

sanskrit: u̱tāśi̍ṣṭhā̱ anu̍ śṛṇvanti̱ vahna̍yaḥ sa̱bheyo̱ vipro̍ bharate ma̱tī dhanā̍ | vī̱ḻu̱dveṣā̱ anu̱ vaśa̍ ṛ̱ṇam ā̍da̱diḥ sa ha̍ vā̱jī sa̍mi̱the brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̍ḥ ||
english: The carriers, those who stand above, hear and follow; the eloquent sage brings wealth with his prayer in the assembly. He exacted the debt at will of those who hate firmly — Brahmaṇaspati is truly the prize-winner in the battle.

sanskrit: brahma̍ṇa̱s pate̍r abhavad yathāva̱śaṁ sa̱tyo ma̱nyur mahi̱ karmā̍ kariṣya̱taḥ ||  | yo gā u̱dāja̱t sa di̱ve vi cā̍bhajan ma̱hīva̍ rī̱tiḥ śava̍sāsara̱t pṛtha̍k ||
english: It happened as Brahmaṇaspati willed — the true wrath of the one about to perform the great deed. He who drove out the cows, he divided them among the heavens; like a great stream it flowed forth separately by power.

sanskrit: brahma̍ṇas pate su̱yama̍sya vi̱śvahā̍ rā̱yaḥ syā̍ma ra̱thyo̱3̱̍ vaya̍svataḥ | vī̱reṣu̍ vī̱rām̐ upa̍ pṛṅdhi na̱s tvaṁ yad īśā̍no̱ brahma̍ṇā̱ veṣi̍ me̱ hava̍m ||
english: O Brahmaṇaspati, may we be always in possession of easily controlled wealth that has offspring; masters of the chariot, full of vigour. Mix the hero among heroes for us — thou who art lord and dost heed my call with thy prayer.

sanskrit: brahma̍ṇas pate̱ tvam a̱sya ya̱ntā sū̱ktasya̍ bodhi̱ tana̍yaṁ ca jinva | viśva̱ṁ tad bha̱draṁ yad ava̍nti de̱vā bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: O Brahmaṇaspati, be thou the controller of this hymn; be aware, and quicken its offspring. All that is blessed which the gods protect — may we speak forth greatly in the assembly, with noble sons.
